title: Oncall escalation: rapid ops notes (pre-call)
content:
Purpose
- Rapid prep for customer-facing escalation call (Acct: BrightLayer) after sustained latency increase on dedicated pool. Quick single-page notes I can bring into the 1pm bridge.

High-level summary (one-liner)
- 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC: BrightLayer reported ~3x tail latency on text-generation endpoints on rwd-dedicated-us-east-2; error rates low but user-facing timeouts at 500ms SLO causing client retries.

People / roles for bridge (call starts 13:00 local)
- Bridge lead (me): Kyra Patel -> coordinate comms, decisions, postmortem owner
- SRE escalation: Noah Chen -> live metric dashboards, RD to correlate infra changes
- Model/runtime engineer: Sana Iqbal -> model variant/quantization checks, perf regressions
- Support lead (customer comms): Maya Ruiz (CS) -> handle customer updates and transcripts
- Oncall infra backup: Arjun Rao -> capacity & autoscale overrides

Pre-call quick checklist (things to have ready)
- Dashboards open: dedicated-pool-latency, per-replica CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, prefix-cache hit rate
- Logs: last 60m request traces (trace ids for 10 slowest requests)
- Recent deploys: check release-engineering activity (last 24h) -> PR #987 (serving runtime) show a small kernel change (linked)
- Resource actions: SSH keys + sudo for autoscale override, kube credentials (sre-sesh)
- Customer context: BrightLayer traffic table (prod-v2 route), sample failing request ids from support thread

Agenda (13:00 - 13:30)
- 13:00-13:03: quick intros + objectives (me)
- 13:03-13:08: SRE telemetry summary (Noah) -> latency histograms, tail spikes, infra alarms
- 13:08-13:12: Runtime/model check (Sana) -> recent model changes, quantization, cache eviction rates
- 13:12-13:18: Immediate mitigation options (all) -> quick config changes we can attempt in 5-15m
- 13:18-13:25: Communication plan (Maya + Kyra) -> customer message + ETA
- 13:25-13:30: Actions & owners + timeboxed follow-ups

Quick investigation notes (to paste into call)
- Observed: 99.9th percentile latency rose from 230ms -> 720ms between 08:50-09:15 UTC; CPU GPU usage not saturated (avg GPU 62%), queue depth increased from 3 -> 18 -> indicates possible batching/backpressure issue
- Cache: prefix cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 41% at 08:49; correlate with eviction logs -> TTLs reduced by a maintenance job?
- Recent PRs: PR #987 changed kernel reorder heuristic; sanity-check diff shows new path that may disable a fast path for some seq lengths.
- Errors: application errors stable (<0.01%); user-visible timeouts driven by queuing, not model OOMs.

Immediate mitigations (ranked by risk/impact)
- 1) Route BrightLayer traffic to a fallback model variant (v2-quantized) with slightly higher latency but lower queueing sensitivity. Risk: possible quality variance. Time: <5m to update routing rule. Owner: Kyra.
- 2) Increase dedicated pool replica count by +2 (scale override). Risk: cost, warmup latency. Time: ~6-10m. Owner: Arjun.
- 3) Temporarily reduce batch-size upper bound in runtime config to limit accumulation. Risk: throughput drop, may increase CPU. Time: ~3-7m. Owner: Sana.
- 4) Roll back PR #987 on a canary subset if correlation confirmed. Risk: potential regression elsewhere. Time: 20-30m. Owner: Noah + Release Eng.

Customer comms (draft to send via Maya)
- Short note (first update): "We’re investigating an elevated latency profile affecting some requests on your dedicated pool. We have a team actively triaging and will follow up with an ETA for mitigation within 15 minutes."
- Follow-up (post-mitigation): include root cause hypothesis and timeline for postmortem delivery.

Runbook commands / check snippets (copy-paste during call)
- Top slow traces (kusto): kusto> traces | where service=="rwd-serving" and timestamp > ago(60m) | order by duration desc | limit 10
- Check cache evictions: curl -s http://metrics.internal/cache?pool=rwd-dedicated-us-east-2 | jq .evictions_last_hour
- Scale override (kube): kubectl scale deployment/rwd-dedicated --replicas=8 -n prod || notify Arjun
- Route update (console CLI): rwdctl route update --customer BrightLayer --route prod-v2 --model v2-quantized --priority temporary

Open questions / hypotheses to test during call
- Did maintenance job change TTLs or cache config around 08:45? (check infra change log)
- Is PR #987 causally linked to disabled fast path for 512-token seqs? Need quick diff review + perf test on canary.
- Are client-side retry patterns amplifying queuing (observed spikes align with client retry bursts)?

Post-call action items (template we will capture on the call)
- Action: Apply routing change -> Owner: Kyra -> Due: 2026-03-12T13:10Z -> Status: pending
- Action: Scale + monitor 10m -> Owner: Arjun -> Due: 2026-03-12T13:20Z -> Status: pending
- Action: Reproduce perf locally w/ PR #987 on canary -> Owner: Sana -> Due: 2026-03-12T14:30Z -> Status: pending
- Action: Customer update sent + transcript posted -> Owner: Maya -> Due: 2026-03-12T13:15Z -> Status: pending
- Postmortem owner: Kyra -> Draft due by 2026-03-15 -> Include timeline, root cause, and mitigation plan

Notes to self / call tactics
- Keep messages short and timeboxed; prioritize action over deep diagnosis during initial bridge.
- If we pick routing fallback, confirm SLO/QA tradeoffs with Maya before applying.
- Capture all decisions in the incident ticket (JIRA-1234) and label as "brightlayer-latency-20260312".

Scratchpad (things to copy into FAQ for customer later)
- What changed: kernel heuristic (PR #987) + transient cache eviction spike (TTL misconfig change during infra maintenance) -> combined effect increased queueing for some seq lengths
- Why route helps: fallback model has more stable batching path (different kernel) and higher cache hit due to warmed prefixes
- Long-term fixes: revert heuristic or add canary gating + monitor cache TTL pushes + automated warmup on pool scale events

End of notes
- Quick check: confirm Maya online at 12:55; ping Noah at 12:58 to share live dashboards.

Unresolved (post-call)
- Confirm exact infra change that reduced TTLs and whether it was intentional (ask infra-owner: infra-ops/maintenance ticket).
- Perf regression reproducibility across seq length distributions (Sana).
